differentiation.occupancy_preservation: The negative directed KL rewards distinguishable endpoint assignment distributions rather than a shared codeword; gradients move codewords to increase the target-to-source assignment divergence. The reverse KL is not included, so exchanging endpoints changes the objective. The balance penalty moves underused source-assignment probability upward and overused probability downward across the batch; neither term directly attracts the two endpoints' codewords.

vs_r8.why: Unlike the inert encoder-only terms, soft assignment probabilities depend directly on the codebook and give it a gradient. Unlike the collapsed pairwise cross-entropy, the information term rewards differing endpoint assignments rather than making both endpoints select the same code; the separate marginal penalty targets usage balance instead of pairwise codeword convergence.

differentiation.vs_reference_arm: the reference arm is the untouched host; this candidate adds one term whose gradient reaches the codebook without pulling a transition's two codewords together

equation: For each valid row i, define p^s_ij = softmax_j(-||source_i-codebook_j||_2^2 / tau) and p^t_ij = softmax_j(-||target_i-codebook_j||_2^2 / tau). Let q^s_j = mean_i p^s_ij and u_j = 1/C. Minimize L = -lambda_info * mean_i KL(p^t_i || p^s_i) + lambda_balance * KL(u || q^s).
expected_failure_modes: Maximizing directed KL can make endpoint assignments artificially different, sacrificing pair-level ER or useful sequence structure. The batch-level balance penalty may also balance soft usage without balancing hard assignments, or become noisy when a batch poorly represents the catalogue.

forbidden_substitutions.reason: a quota on the assignment is the family that produced 39.5% and 24.2% occupancy without preserving the exported codes
a term that pulls a pair's two codewords together is what collapsed the level-0 codebook to two codes

hypotheses: The candidate is falsified if exchanging source and target leaves the measured loss unchanged, if codebook gradients are zero or non-finite, or if the frozen export fails to raise pair-level Hard-L1 ER while meeting the control thresholds for level-0 Gini, prefix branches, train-to-test frequency drift, and sequence information.

symbols.KL(p || q): Kullback-Leibler divergence from distribution p to distribution q.
symbols.i: Batch-row index, restricted to rows where mask is true.
symbols.p^s_i: Soft source assignment distribution for row i.
symbols.p^t_i: Soft target assignment distribution for row i.
symbols.q^s_j: Batch-mean source assignment probability for codebook entry j.
symbols.source_i: Source endpoint embedding for row i.
symbols.target_i: Target endpoint embedding for row i.
symbols.u_j: Uniform target usage probability, equal to 1/C.
